explain.say: Look at the first dot. In 196 BCE, priests carved a message on this stone three times: in hieroglyphs, in an everyday Egyptian script called Demotic, and in ancient Greek. Same message, three ways. Can you see why that helps?

explain.say: Jump to 1799. French soldiers near the town of Rashid, which Europeans called Rosetta, dug up the stone. Scholars could read the Greek part at once. Now they had a crib, like an answer sheet for a puzzle. What would you do next?

explain.say: See this dot? Thomas Young, a British scientist, noticed some hieroglyphs sat inside oval rings called cartouches. They spelled royal names, like Ptolemy. So some signs must stand for sounds! Could you spell your name in sound signs?

explain.say: And here is the winner. In 1822, Jean-Francois Champollion, who also knew Coptic, a later form of Egyptian, cracked the code. Fantastic work, detective! Wow: it is the most visited object in the British Museum, and many in Egypt want it back.

faq.q: What is written on the Rosetta Stone?
faq.a: A decree from 196 BCE praising King Ptolemy V, written by priests. The same text appears in hieroglyphs, Demotic script and ancient Greek.
asks: What does the Rosetta Stone say?

faq.a: French soldiers found it in 1799 near Rashid, a town in Egypt's Nile Delta, during Napoleon's campaign in Egypt.
asks: Where was the Rosetta Stone found?

faq.q: Why is the Rosetta Stone in London?
faq.a: When Britain defeated the French in Egypt in 1801, the stone was handed over under a treaty and reached the British Museum in 1802. Many Egyptians would like it returned.
asks: Why does Britain have the Rosetta Stone?

faq.a: He compared the Greek text with the hieroglyphs, starting with royal names, and used his knowledge of Coptic. He showed that signs can stand for sounds as well as ideas.
A cartouche is an oval ring drawn around a king's or queen's name in hieroglyphs. Cartouches helped decoders find names like Ptolemy and Cleopatra.
asks: What are the oval rings in hieroglyphs?

facts: The Rosetta Stone carries one decree from 196 BCE in hieroglyphs, Demotic and ancient Greek.
Champollion announced his decipherment of hieroglyphs in 1822.
The stone was found in 1799 near Rashid, called Rosetta by Europeans, in Egypt.

options.show: It had the same text in Greek

quiz.why: Scholars could read the Greek, so they could match it against the hieroglyphs.

wrong.1: There was no dictionary, just one decree written three ways.
wrong.2: Champollion lived about 2,000 years after it was carved.

quiz.say: Who announced in 1822 that he had decoded hieroglyphs?
quiz.why: Jean-Francois Champollion cracked the code in 1822.

wrong.1: Napoleon led the army in Egypt but decoded nothing.
wrong.2: Ptolemy V was the king the decree praised in 196 BCE.
